#en: First time I docked here, I thought it was just another junkyard orbiting the edge of nowhere. Now I cannot shake the feeling that this depot is where the story started, even if nobody remembers the first telling. Every Deadspace loader I talk to starts their version with, "I heard from a guy who heard it from a crew that is gone now," and the details never match, just the punchline: ships that jump out fat and healthy, never ping another beacon, and leave behind drive logs that look like they were written by the same careful hand. The corrupted files I pulled at that remote rock and the whispers from the broken yard point back here, but whatever really happened the first time someone "tested to failure" in this place has already been chewed into rumor. All that is left is the pattern, and the quiet way these people lower their voices when they think the depot itself might be listening.
zh: 我第一次在这里停靠时，以为它不过是又一座绕着天涯边缘转的废品站。如今我却甩不掉一个念头：这个补给站就是故事开始的地方，哪怕没人记得最早的讲述。我聊过的每一个死寂空间装卸工，开场白都是"我听一个哥们说的，那哥们又是听一支如今没了的船队说的"，细节从来对不上，只有那句包袱一样：飞船满载健康地跃出去，从此再没打过一次信标，留下的驱动日志像是同一只谨慎的手写出来的。我在那块偏远岩石上提取的损坏文件、还有那座破船坞里传出的低语，都指回这里；可当年第一次有人在这地方"测到失效"时究竟发生了什么，早已被嚼成了传闻。剩下的只有那图案，以及这些人一觉得补给站本身可能在听时，就压低声音的安静模样。

#en: I am not saying I know where she is, just that the pattern is wrong. I have been stuck on this rusting module for three tours watching traffic for Ryujin, and data does not just decide to jump manifests on its own. The archive pulls show a neat little chain of thefts, then one transfer hits this node and comes out sliced, like someone reached in with a scalpel and rerouted only the parts they cared about. One of the techs swears he saw an old bionics prefix in the checksum, the kind tied to that shuttered lab they swore was scrubbed years ago. Another tech says that prefix is a ghost tag, leftover junk, that we are all seeing shadows because of the stories about a red-haired doc and melted implants. All I know is: every time code goes missing around her name, it leaves the same faint trace, and this time the trace points straight at that dead bionics facility everyone pretends not to remember.
zh: 我不是说我知道她在哪儿，我只是说这个图案不对劲。我为龙神盯着交通数据，被困在这个锈迹斑斑的模块上已经三个任期了，而数据不会自己决定在清单间跳来跳去。档案调取记录显示一串整整齐齐的小盗窃，随后有一次传输打在这个节点上，出来时却被切开了，像有人拿着手术刀伸进来，只改道了他们关心的那部分。有个技工赌咒说，他在校验和里看到过一个旧的仿生学前缀，正是他们赌咒说几年前就已经清洗掉的那座关闭实验室用的那种。另一个技工说那前缀是个幽灵标签、是遗留垃圾，说我们全是因为那些关于红发医生与熔化植入物的故事在看见影子。我只知道：每当代码在跟她名字有关的地方失踪，留下的都是同样微弱的痕迹——而这一次，痕迹直指那座人人都假装不记得的废弃仿生学设施。

#en: I have been sitting in this cramped berth on The Den long enough to know why nobody volunteers for this posting. Everything is beige and half-asleep, the kind of place where reports get filed, stamped, and then quietly forgotten. Which is exactly why whoever hid those numbers chose it. If you want something buried, you do not drop it in a warzone; you tuck it under a bored clerk in a dead system and let routine smother it.\n\nThe stories I picked up on the way here all sound like they have been passed around too many tables. A hauler that was there, then was not. A rigger who saves people in one version and strands them in another. Every time someone tells it, the edges get rounded off, the guilt spread thinner. But underneath the smoke and barroom bravado, the same outline keeps showing through. Missing crews, altered manifests, and a line of drift that curves back toward the same invisible hand.
zh: 我在巢穴站的这间逼仄铺位上坐得太久，久到我知道为什么没人自愿接这个岗位。一切都是米黄色的、半睡不醒的，那种报告被归档、盖章、然后悄悄遗忘的地方。而这正是藏起那些数字的人选中它的原因。你要是想把什么埋掉，就别把它丢进战区；把它塞给一个死气沉沉星系里百无聊赖的文员，让例行公事把它闷死。\n\n我一路听来的那些故事，听起来都像被太多张桌子传来传去过。一艘本来在那里的货船，然后不在了。一名装配工，在一个版本里救人，在另一个版本里把人扔下不管。每被讲一次，棱角就被磨圆一点，罪责就摊得更薄。可在那层烟幕和酒馆式的逞强底下，同一个轮廓始终透出来。失踪的船员、被改动的清单，以及一条总朝同一只看不见的手弯回去的漂移线。

#en: I was supposed to be gone before the storm rolled in. Just a simple refill, a few signatures, then back to hauling grain where the worst thing that happens is a clogged pump. Instead I am sitting in the office watching the wind shove dust against the viewport while the consoles spit out half-finished reports and error flags that no one ever cleared. Someone rushed through this place in a hurry, cut corners in the logs, pushed a few ships through on backdoor clearances, then ran before the numbers could catch up. The ledgers are messy in a very precise way, like a hand that knows exactly which fields matter and which can be left wrong for years without anyone noticing. I am no investigator, but even I can see the pattern of diverted routes and vanished transponders threaded through this depot, and it has me checking over my shoulder every time the comms crackle with another "routine" traffic update.
zh: 我本该在风暴卷来之前就走的。不过是简单补个燃料、签几个名，然后回去运粮食——那份活儿里最糟的情况也就是泵堵了。可现在我却坐在办公室里，看着风把沙尘推上观察窗，控制台吐出一份份没写完的报告和从未有人清除过的错误标记。有人匆匆忙忙地从这地方过了一遍，在日志里抄了近路，用后门许可放行了几艘船，然后在数字追上来之前就跑了。那些账簿乱得很精准，像一只清楚知道哪些字段要紧、哪些可以错着好几年而无人察觉的手。我不是什么调查员，可连我都看得出这片补给站里穿插着被改道航线和消失应答器的图案，每次通讯里噼啪传来又一则"例行"交通更新，我都会忍不住回头看一眼。

#en: I am still shaking dust out of my hair from this bunker, and the consoles are older than half the patrol grid, but they still know how to keep a secret. The deserter was sloppy with his deletions; he scrubbed the export paths, not the cached scans. Buried under old meteor tracks and shuttle noise, I found a sequence of atmospheric spikes that do not belong to any registered thruster profile, cutting straight across restricted lanes like they owned the sky. Cross-checking the timestamps against patrol rosters gives me a heading and a hull class, and every line points toward a Navy combat ship that was never supposed to be on that circuit at all. Some of the techs back in the dive swear they saw it slip past on a dead transponder; others say it is all barroom exaggeration. Either way, the next piece of this mess is sitting in a silent UC hulk, waiting for someone brave or desperate enough to board it.
zh: 我头发里还抖得出这座碉堡里的灰，这里的控制台比半个巡逻网格都要老，可它们仍然懂得怎么保守秘密。那名逃兵删东西时很马虎；他擦掉了导出路径，却没擦掉缓存的扫描。在旧流星轨迹和穿梭机噪声底下，我找到了一连串大气尖峰，不属于任何登记过的推进器剖面，笔直横切受限航道，仿佛这片天空是它们家的。把时间戳与巡逻名册交叉比对，我得到了一个航向和一个船体级别，每一条线都指向一艘本不该出现在那条航线上的海军战斗舰。潜水区那边的几个技工赌咒说，他们见过它开着死应答器悄悄溜过；另一些人说那全是酒馆里的夸大其词。无论怎样，这摊烂摊子的下一块拼图正躺在一具沉默的联殖船壳里，等着哪个够勇敢或够绝望的人登上去。

#en: This module has a way of hanging onto things it is not supposed to. Old firmware, obsolete protocols, ghost accounts from contractors nobody remembers hiring it is all still here, just pushed one layer deeper every time someone does a "cleanup." I came in thinking I was tracing a straightforward breach, another bored tech moving proprietary routes offsite for a quiet sale. But the deeper I dug, the more I kept finding the same bent curves pressed into different logs, like a bootprint stamped over and over in fresh dust. Someone upstream noticed, tried to wipe it, then stopped halfway through, like they got called away or decided they did not want their name tied to this anymore. This place remembers them anyway. Even with lazy edits and truncated records, the system still clings to their mistakes and to the shape of those impossible paths, faint and overlapping where no sane corridor should ever cross.
zh: 这个模块有一种本事，能留住它本不该留住的东西。旧固件、作废的协议、来自没人记得雇过的承包商的幽灵账户——全都还在，只是每次有人做一次"清理"，就被往下推深一层。我来的时候以为自己只是在追查一次简单的入侵，又一个百无聊赖的技工把专有航线挪到站外去悄悄变卖。可我挖得越深，越是在不同的日志里一遍遍撞见同样那些弯曲的弧线，像一枚靴印被反复盖在新落的灰尘上。上游有人察觉了，想把它擦掉，却在半途停下，像被叫走了，或者打定主意不想再让自己的名字跟这事绑在一起。可这地方照样记着他们。哪怕有偷懒的删改和被截断的记录，系统仍死死攥着他们的错误，攥着那些不可能路径的形状——淡淡的、相互交叠，没有任何理智的走廊会从那里穿过。

#en: I keep telling myself I only take the night shifts in the back corridors because the pay is better, but it is really because no one looks too hard back here. You sign off a crate as medical relief, watch it roll past the scanners, and by the time it hits storage someone has scraped the tags and called it scrap. Lately, though, the routes stamped on the cargo slates do not match the traffic boards upstairs, little course corrections that nudge whole loads away from the usual lanes. Some of the other handlers swear they saw a woman in a battered flight jacket, just standing at the junctions, fingertip tracing invisible paths on the bulkhead, but when I ask for details they laugh it off like bar talk. Maybe it is all exaggeration, but the manifests keep changing after she is supposed to have passed through, and the colony destinations on those shipments have a way of disappearing from the system altogether.
zh: 我一直告诉自己，我只挑后走廊的夜班是因为钱多，其实真正的原因是这里没人会细看。你把一只板条箱签成医疗救济品，看着它滚过扫描仪，等它进到仓库时，已经有人刮掉了标签、管它叫废料。可最近，货板上盖印的航线跟楼上的交通公示板对不上，一些小小的航向修正把整批货从惯常航道推偏。别的几个装卸工赌咒说，他们见过一个穿破旧飞行夹克的女人，就站在岔口那儿，指尖在舱壁上描着看不见的路径；可我一追问细节，他们就当酒吧闲话一笑而过。也许那全是夸大的说法，可每次她该经过之后，清单都会变，而那些货运单上的殖民目的地，总有办法从系统里整个消失。

#en: I spent half the cycle today under New Atlantis instead of in it, sitting in a humming archive room that smells like old ozone and cheaper coffee than they serve upstairs. One junior admin owed someone a favor and let me mirror a set of deprecated traffic models he swore nobody used anymore. The projections looked clean at first, then I started overlaying real freight logs. Tiny manual corrections, always in the same direction, always just enough to miss something the official charts do not admit is there. When I asked who signed off on those edits, every analyst I cornered said the same thing they had only seen the pattern after someone else ran it, and nobody was willing to say whose name was on the original run. There were other gaps too, places in their stories where words should have been and were not, like they had all agreed ahead of time which parts of the night sky did not belong in the conversation.
zh: 今天我大半个周期都待在新亚特兰蒂斯底下，而不是里面，坐在一间嗡嗡作响的档案室里，那地方闻起来是旧臭氧和比楼上供应得还廉价的咖啡味。有个初级管理员欠某人一个人情，让我镜像了一套他赌咒说早没人用的作废交通模型。那些投影起初看着很干净，随后我开始把真实的货运日志叠上去。微小的手动修正，永远朝着同一个方向，永远刚好足以避开官方星图不肯承认存在的东西。我问是谁批准了那些改动，每一个被我堵住的资深分析师都说了同样的话：他们只是照别人跑过的结果才看出来有图案；而没人愿意说出最初那次运行的署名是谁。还有别的空白，他们叙述中的一些地方本该有词却没有，像他们早就一致约定好了，夜空里的哪些部分不该被放进这场谈话里。

#en:
I am writing this down so I can stop replaying it in my head every time the grav drive spins up.

The buoy was supposed to be scrap, just another hazard marker drifting where nobody cares. I cracked it for parts and the data core spilled out a set of routes that should not exist, drift math nudged off by the same fraction every time. When I asked around on the dock, nobody claimed to know anything; they just said they had heard it from a friend, from a cousin, from some pilot who had already shipped out. Same name, different mouths, nobody willing to swear they were the first.

Dock records do not match the departure times. A freighter listed as lost took a path that never appeared on the official chart. Every time I try to trace the origin of those vectors, the line bends back into rumor and shrugs. It feels like catching a voice in the static and being told, over and over, that someone else heard it first.
zh:
我把这个记下来，好让自己不必每次重力驱动一转起来就在脑子里重放它。

那只浮标本该是废料，不过又一个漂在没人管的地方的危险标记。我把它拆了取零件，数据核里却泄出一组本不该存在的航线，漂移算法每次都偏掉同样的一个小分数。我在码头上打听时，没人承认知道什么；他们只说是从一个朋友那儿听来的，从一个表亲那儿，从某个已经出航走了的飞行员那儿。同样的名字，不同的嘴，没人肯起誓说自己是最先知道的那个。

码头记录与离港时间对不上。一艘被列为失事的货船走的是一条从未出现在官方星图上的路径。每次我试图追查那些矢量的源头，线就弯回传闻和耸肩里。感觉就像在静电中逮住一个声音，然后被人一遍又一遍地告知：别人早就先听到了。

#en: I am logging this while the tug's reactor is still warm under my boots, before some supervisor edits the story into something cleaner. We were supposed to mark the derelict and move on, just another piece of junk drifting a few clicks off the lane. Then Nav said its drift did not match the model, Comms swore the beacon was just standard hazard code, and I said we did not have time to argue over scrap. Three different readings, three different priorities, and we split the difference like idiots. By the time we were close enough to see the extra plating and the way the drones orbited it like guard dogs, every channel on the board was full of that same faint, wrong signature. I keep thinking if I had pushed harder, or if Comms had not muted that one warning ping to clear space for a routine check-in, we would not have watched a whole cargo stack vanish off our scopes as if the lane itself opened a door and swallowed it.
zh: 我趁拖船的反应堆在我靴子底下还热乎时记下这段，免得某个主管把这段经过改写成更干净的东西。我们本该给那艘弃船做个标记就走，不过是又一堆漂在航道外几公里处的垃圾。可导航说它的漂移跟模型对不上，通讯赌咒说那信标只是标准危险代码，而我说我们没时间为废料吵架。三种不同的读数，三种不同的优先级，而我们像白痴一样各让一步。等我们靠得够近，看清那多出来的装甲板、看清那些无人机像看门狗一样绕着它转时，控制台上每一个频道都塞满了同样微弱、不对劲的信号。我总在想，要是我当时再坚持一下，或者通讯没有为了腾出例行报到的空档而把那一记警告嗡鸣调成静音，我们就不至于眼睁睁看着一整摞货物从示波器上消失——仿佛那条航道自己开了一扇门，把它吞了进去。

#en: I docked today at what should have been a dead node on the edge of nowhere. Old UC paint, dead beacon, the sort of relay you route around because nobody has maintained it since before you were born. Except the boards down in the well are still listening, running just enough juice to catch a little kick in the traffic a crooked bump in the timing that does not belong to age or dust. Silk Collective types are squatting here, running contraband through the blind spot, muttering about "lucky" jumps and refusing to look too closely at the diagnostics. Every time I ask about the missing convoy, voices drop, conversations thin out, like speaking the details aloud might ping the wrong set of ears. All I have right now is this whisper in the numbers, a relay that was supposed to be cold, and the memory of that analyst on Jemison who said her anomaly folders emptied themselves and then refused to say anything else above a murmur.
zh: 我今天停靠在一个本该是天涯尽头的死节点上。旧联殖涂装、死信标，那种你会绕开的通讯中继——自你出生以前就没人维护过。可下面井里的主板还在听着，耗着刚够的电流，捕捉交通中一点小小的踢动，一处不属于年岁或灰尘的歪斜顿挫。丝绸集体那伙人正赖在这里，把违禁品从盲区里运过，嘟囔着什么"幸运"跃迁，还拒绝细看诊断数据。每次我问起那支失踪的运输队，声音就低下去，谈话就稀薄起来，仿佛把细节说出口会惊动错的耳朵。我现在手里只有这些数字里的低语、一座本该冰冷的通讯中继，以及杰米森星上那位分析师的记忆——她说她的异常文件夹自己清空了，然后就再也不肯把话说得比耳语大声。
